title: feat(spec)!: a multi-package artifact carries its metadata once, in packages[] (#14512)
body:
Fixes #14512

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

The emitter half of ADR-0130 D4 option B, ruled on #14512 (maintainer, decision batch #23, 2026-09-03, comment 5528589044): **readers first, emitter last**. `composeStacks(…, { manifest: 'preserve' })` stops emitting the flattened top-level collections for a multi-package artifact, so each definition is serialized once, under the package that owns it.

## The measurement the dispatch ordered first, and which fork it selected

Triage's 置信缺口 asked whether the collections inside a `packages[i]` body have the **same shape** as the flattened top level, because if they differ, option B is a shape adaptation and the ruling's cost estimate has to be re-ordered. Measured on `origin/main` `80ca0b1c88`, three ways:

1. **Declaration identity — 35/35 keys are the SAME object.** `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.shape` ∩ `AssembledPackageBodySchema.shape` is 35 keys, and for every one of them the two shapes hold the *identical schema object* (`top[k] === body[k]`), because `assembledPackageBodyShape()` copies the entries of `STACK_DEFINITION_COLLECTIONS_SHAPE` that the stack schema also spreads. There is one declaration per collection, not two that happen to agree.
2. **The key sets differ only outside the collections.** The body additionally carries 20 manifest identity fields (`id`, `name`, `version`, `type`, `namespace`, `scope`, `engines`, …). Eleven top-level keys have no body expression and are the artifact envelope: `api`, `devHint`, `devLogins`, `devPlugins`, `i18n`, `manifest`, `onEnable`, `packages`, `plugins`, `runtimeModule`, `server`. Those eleven are exactly what this change keeps at the top level.
3. **Data level.** On `examples/app-multi-package` the top-level collections were an identical multiset to the union of the bodies (`apps` 1 = 1, `objects` 2 = 2). On the two-package collection zoo (`packages/cli/test/fixtures/option-b-collection-zoo.ts`), all 11 populated families identical, 0 differing.

⇒ **Same shape. Option B is "iterate somewhere else", and the emitter change proceeds.**

Two content facts measured beside the shape, both about `objects` and both already known to the ruling (5521308880): under `objectConflict: 'merge'` the top level carries a merged object no body carries, and a standalone action bound to a *sibling package's* object is merged into the top-level object only. Those are composition-time derivations of the flattened copy, not a different shape of any collection — and they are the double source of truth the ruling refused to keep.

## The mechanical re-verification of the reader program

`5557596712`'s all-clear is a card-state reading and says so. The program's own criterion is #15004's acceptance probe, run here rather than inferred: `packages/cli/test/option-b-reader-acceptance.pin.test.ts`, which boots a two-package collection zoo through every load boundary in both shapes.

- Run on `origin/main` `80ca0b1c88` **before any edit**: `Test Files 1 passed / Tests 9 passed`. All **38 probe rows present on both legs, 0 lost**, `OPTION_B_LOSSES` empty, five boundaries represented. No still-red subsystem, so no seventh reader card is owed.
- Re-run with this PR's emitter landed: the same 9 pass, 38 rows, 0 lost.

## What a top-level-only reader now sees, and the size

`examples/app-multi-package`, built with `os build` on both sides of the change (the spec source flipped to the base commit, spec rebuilt, artifact rebuilt, then restored and rebuilt — restore verified by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`):

| | top-level keys | `dist/objectstack.json` |
|:--|:--|--:|
| before | `apps, manifest, objects, packages` | 8,223 B |
| after | `manifest, packages` | 5,328 B (−35.2%) |

A consumer that only ever read the top level sees **no collections at all** for a multi-package artifact — the change is breaking for it, which is what `Clause-②: yes` and the changeset's `**BREAKING**` banner declare. Every reader this repository ships was converted first and reads through `packages[]`; an artifact built *before* this change still carries both halves and still loads, because D4's read-both rule is untouched. `os build`'s own summary is unchanged (`Data: 2 Objects 5 Fields · UI: 1 Apps`) and its three author-time findings are the same three, in a different order (the union rule input is derived from package order now).

One behaviour that moves for the better, measured on the probe's compiled-artifact leg: a seed dataset declared once reached the runtime's shared seed registry **twice** on the additive artifact (the body copy is stamped `_packageId`/`_provenance` by registration before the collection resolver compares it, so the top-level copy's identity claim misses) and reaches it **once** now.

## The three conditions that keep this a copy-removal

`packagesCarryEveryInputCollection` and `packagesReproduceComposedCollections` strip only when all three hold, and each is pinned:

- **Two or more package entries** — ADR-0130 D7 as a condition rather than a promise: a single-package artifact is byte-identical to before.
- **Every input's collections attributed to a body** — an input with no `manifest` has no package to own its collections (`manifest` is optional on the stack schema), and an input that carries `packages` contributes those entries untouched, so its own collections belong to no body. Either shape keeps today's additive output, which every reader still reads. Neither is refused: a composition that was legal before stays legal.
- **The bodies reproduce the composed collections** — ⭐ added after the at-tier review measured the first two insufficient. Conditions 1 and 2 read the INPUT stacks; what the strip deletes is the **COMPOSED** result, and those differ wherever composition reconciled something. `packagesReproduceComposedCollections` asks the question the strip actually depends on — does the union of the bodies reproduce the flattened collections, item for item — as multiset equality over a stable serialization per package-owned key, mirroring `@objectstack/runtime`'s own `stableIdentity` so producer and reader cannot disagree. Deliberately **not** array-order equality: a `packages[]` artifact registers in topological order, and requiring order would keep the copy where nothing is lost. Two shapes fail it and keep the additive output: an `objectConflict: 'merge'`/`'override'` collision, where the flattened half is the **reconciled** copy; and a standalone action bound by `mergeActionsIntoObjects` onto an object a **sibling** package owns, where no name collides at all and the flattened half still is not a copy. The strip also moved to after `mergeActionsIntoObjects`, so what it tests is what that step produced rather than an earlier draft.

## Verification

- **Ablation (reverse verification), with the MUTATION named because the count depends on it.** Replacing the `packagesReproduceComposedCollections` conjunct with `true` and re-running: the five changed spec files go **`3 failed | 103 passed (106)`** — the failures are exactly the three new cases (merge, override, sibling-binding) — and the runtime consumer pin goes **`1 failed | 14 passed`**, failing with `expected [ …(2) ] to have a length of 1 but got 2`. Baselines on the same files are `106 passed` and `15 passed`, both exit 0. Ablating conditions 2 and 3 together instead gives `6 failed | 100 passed`. ⚠️ Earlier revisions of this body quoted `2 failed | 34 passed` and then `5 failed | 98 passed`; **neither reproduces against the mutation and file set named here**, because each was taken over a different pair of the two. The criterion is load-bearing either way — that is what the ablation establishes — but an ablation count is exactly the kind of claim that must not be inherited, so this body now carries the mutation, the file set and the baseline alongside the number. Tree restored and verified clean after each leg.
- **Tests** (exit codes captured before any pipe, each through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, whose `VERDICT` line is the reading): `@objectstack/spec` 511 files / 14,934 tests; `@objectstack/cli` unit tier 222 files / 3,141 tests; `@objectstack/metadata` 53/792; `@objectstack/objectql` 303/5,050; `@objectstack/runtime` 272/3,799; `@objectstack/plugin-security` 117/2,250; `@objectstack/plugin-dev` 8/76; `@objectstack/verify` 15/116; `@objectstack/core` 51/1,321; `@objectstack/dogfood` `multi-package-artifact.dogfood.test.ts` 9/9 — all green. `typecheck` green for spec, cli, metadata, plugin-security, plugin-dev.
- **Gate families**: derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (120 families, from the merge-base change set, not a hand-written list) and reconciled with `--ran`: **120 derived, 120 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**, every family recorded with its own exit code. Two needed a prerequisite build first (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n-coverage` — exit 3, not a finding) and one needed `@objectstack/client-react` built (`check:skill-examples`); all three are green after building what they name. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — all 15 generated artifacts up to date, nothing to regenerate. `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` exit 0; `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` exit 0, reading this changeset as `[BREAKING+clause-②-narrowing]`.
- **Lint, narrowed and declared.** `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 13 lintable changed files: exit 0, 13 files, 0 errors, 1 warning that is `File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied` on the `.mdx` page and is identical on the base revision. The narrowing is sound because this repository runs one `eslint.config.mjs` which **never enables type-aware linting** (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules) for any file — stated in that file's own header at the `QUERY_OPTIONS_TEST_GLOBS` block — so no edit in these files can move the verdict on a file they do not contain. The repo-wide sweep is CI's.

## Landing

⚠️ **This diff touches a governed surface: `docs/adr/0130-release-artifact-as-co-ownership-boundary.md` (Tier H under Prime Directive #14).** The addendum is part of what the ruling ordered for the emitter half, and Prime Directive #13 forbids changing behaviour in ADR-governed territory without the record moving with it, so the two are here together. ⛔ No seat merges, queues or arms auto-merge on this PR: Tier H lifts only for an authorized approval. A contract review at the review tier is owed as well and is the seat's to dispatch against this head — ⛔ not self-reviewed here.

## Acceptance notes

- `packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts` says `#14877` will publish the package-owned key set as an export, at which point three private derivations (that module, `packages/cli/src/utils/stack-collections.ts` and the `packageOwnedCollectionKeys()` added here) read one symbol instead. Noted, not filed here — it is an open card, and nothing in this diff makes it more urgent.
- The `os build` author-time findings arrive in a different ORDER after this change (same three findings, same text). No card: the union rule input is unordered by contract and nothing pins the order.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

**改了什么** —— 多包产物(一个 `objectstack.json` 里装 N 个包)以前把每条元数据写两遍:顶层扁平一份、`packages[]` 每个包体里再一份。现在只写一份,写在拥有它的包里。单包产物一个字节都没动。

**为什么改** —— 两份副本没有任何东西负责对账,合并/覆盖策略下它们已被实测为内容不同,消费者看到哪一份取决于它走了哪个读取方;体积也白涨了 35%(示例实测 8,223 → 5,328 字节)。维护者 2026-09-03 已裁定方向(读取方先改、发射端最后改),读取方六张卡全部落地,本 PR 是最后一步。

**风险与代价(含回滚)** —— 风险面是"某个读取方没被改到",症状是静默的:不报错,集合直接为空。为此本 PR 先跑了 #15004 的验收探针(38 个读取点、两种产物形态、五个装载边界),落地前后都是 0 丢失。已经构建好、躺在客户磁盘上的旧产物不受影响 —— ADR-0130 D4 的"两种形态都读"规则没动。回滚 = 还原 `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` 的这一步(一个 `if` 加两个辅助函数),产物立刻回到两份副本的旧形态,不需要迁移。

**席位意见** ——

**你要做的** —— 这个 PR 动了 `docs/adr/0130-*.md`(Tier H 受管面),按 Prime Directive #14 只有您的批准能让它落地;ADR 附录记的就是您 2026-09-03 那次裁定的执行结果。请看两处:①附录里"D4 的哪一半变了、哪一半没变"的表述是否准确;②「两种组合保持旧形态」这条兜底是否是您要的(没有 manifest 的输入、自带 `packages` 又自带集合的输入,都不剥离,也都不拒绝)。
